cases.name: a whole second: .000 gives .001 (operations.json claim attempt)
no d: the attempt carries no deadline
a fraction of three digits: .100 gives .101
a fraction of four digits, truncated to milliseconds: .1009 gives .101
the last millisecond of a second: .999 gives the next second's .000

attempt_deadlines.description: Wire 6.2, spec 10.2: the deadline an attempt carries, d + 1 ms, for a d the protocol computes for the attempt. d is read at millisecond precision, further digits truncated (wire 1.6), and the deadline is written with three fraction digits; without a d the attempt carries no deadline (null).

description: Every operation type (wire 6.1-6.4) for alice's account at generation 1, signed by its writer over lp("pubky-switch/v1/op", identity, body). Signer operations carry app_id null. Batches share one batch ID and count; cursor.set is unsigned and outside the count. Each record.put value opens with alice's scope key to a record value of the sample protocol tasks, which the switch treats as opaque.

integer_bounds.description: Wire 1.1: every int is a JSON number from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9007199254740991), without sign, fraction or exponent. Each case is the operation named in based_on with its orphan_after written as number, signed again by its writer, so its signature verifies and only the integer rule decides: the largest integer is valid; 2^53, a fraction (86400.0 included), an exponent and a sign are refused with 400 bad_request, before the operation's fields are read. Only the opaque members wire 1.1 names by path are exempt: a message body's metadata, a tasks.done body's proof, an invite code's context (encoding.json json).

invite_context.description: Wire 6.2: an invite code's context is at most 1024 bytes as the writer serialized it, the bytes of its value within the signed body from its first byte to its last, whitespace included, never a re-serialization; else 413 too_large. Each case is the invite_code.put of operations with its context written with spaces inside its object, signed again by the wallet, so its signature verifies and only the length decides. context_bytes is the context as written, compact_bytes compacted.

ops_request.note: POST /v1/{id}/ops body of the registration batch (wire 6.4, spec 12.1 step 2): app.put and the first receive_key.put, then the cursor.

record.put: a write_scopes entry that isn't a scope
cases.rule: record.put: a write_scopes entry isn't a scope (wire 3.1)

shape_rejections.description: Wire 6.2, 6.4 step 9: operations whose shape the service refuses, 400 bad_request, before it compares them with what it holds. Each case is the operation of operations named in based_on with the change its name gives made in its signed body, its record key derived again for the policy it then has (wire 1.5), and signed again by its writer, so its signature verifies and only the shape decides. A record's read_scope, its value_sealed's scope with it, and each write_scopes entry follow the scope rule of wire 3.1 "Scope names"; a key_bundle.put's range starts at data epoch 1 and its first_epoch is at most its last_epoch (wire 3.5, 6.2).

cases.name: unknown member beside a signed operation's body and sig (app.put)
unknown member beside cursor.set's op and position

batch_entries.description: Wire 1.1, 2.2, 6.4: an entry of a POST /ops body has only its own members: a signed operation's carrying form body and sig, a cursor.set its op and position. Each case is the body of ops_request with the member future_restriction added to the entry at the path in member, so every signature still verifies and only the member check refuses it: 400 bad_request, before any signature is checked.

unknown member in a condition's object
unknown member beside a condition's kind
unknown member in the carrying form of record
unknown member in the key bundle

unknown_members.description: Wire 1.1, 6.1: unknown members are refused at every depth of an operation body, as at its top level: in batch, a condition and its object, expected_version, value_sealed, id_inputs, the carrying form of a signed record or cert, and the key bundle. Each case is the operation named in based_on with the member future_restriction added at the path in member (a dotted path; numbers index arrays), signed again by its writer, so its signature verifies and only the member check refuses it: 400 bad_request. The opaque context of invite_code.put is exempt.
